issues.description: trainer_args key mismatch: docstring promises max_steps/val_interval, code reads max_step and never uses val_interval
issues.detail: __init__ reads trainer_args['max_step'] (singular) while the docstring documents 'max_steps'. val_interval is documented but never honored; run() calls valid() every save_interval instead. Callers writing configs to the documented contract will KeyError or get wrong validation cadence. Pick one spelling, honor the documented val_interval, and validate the dict at construction.

issues.description: Checkpoint discovery parses directory names via split('step_')[-1] and crashes on any stray dir
issues.detail: _load_checkpoint globs 'step_*' and sorts by int(name.split('step_')[-1]). A directory named 'step_3_backup' or 'foo_step_10' silently misparses or raises mid-run. Replace string archaeology with a regex full-match (skipping non-matches) or a 'latest' symlink / index.json written at save time.

issues.description: _all_reduce_stats has unstated collective-call discipline and surprising in-place/rebind semantics
issues.detail: The function iterates `for key in stats` issuing one all_reduce per key, requiring every rank to pass identical keys in identical order or NCCL hangs. It also both mutates tensors in-place and rebinds dict entries to new tensors after division, contradicting the 'in-place' docstring. State and enforce the precondition, or return a fresh dict.

issues.description: Specifier strings are a stringly-typed mini-language re-parsed by every consumer
issues.detail: The 'task:name:data_json[:factor]' grammar lives only in argparse --help, with train.py splitting validation specifiers on whitespace and passing train specifiers whole. Paths with colons or spaces silently mishandle. Lift the grammar into a small typed dataclass parser at the CLI boundary so the contract sits in one place.

issues.description: DeepSpeedTrainer silently depends on a global wandb.run with no precondition check
issues.detail: __init__ mutates wandb.config and run() calls wandb.log unconditionally, but there is no assert wandb.run is not None and no injected logger sink. Additionally get_global_grad_norm() can return None on skipped/fp16-overflow steps, polluting or erroring the log. Inject a logger or assert preconditions, and guard None metrics with nan.

issues.description: _load_checkpoint silently falls back to step 0 when an explicit resume_path is missing
issues.detail: If the caller passes a resume_path that does not exist, the code silently starts from scratch rather than raising. Users expecting resumption may waste a full training run. Raise FileNotFoundError when resume_path is explicit and missing; only fall back to auto-discovery when resume_path is unset.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on one root cause: trainer_args is an untyped dict whose documented contract (max_steps, val_interval) diverges from what the code actually reads (max_step) and honors (validation runs every save_interval, not val_interval). Around that core defect, reviewers agree on a cluster of contract and discipline failures: checkpoint discovery parses directory names via fragile string splitting, _all_reduce_stats assumes identical key ordering across ranks without stating or checking the precondition, the CLI relies on a stringly-typed specifier mini-language re-parsed by every consumer, and wandb is a hidden global dependency. Smaller issues — silent resume fallback and unguarded None metrics — should be cleaned up in the same pass. Fix the dict-as-API into a small dataclass with validated keys and most of these vanish.
